Subject: Invoice routing and tax handling for Redwood account

Hi Jonas,

We're getting ready to start billing for our Redwood contract. A couple quick questions so AP can set things up:

- Who will originate the invoices (Redwood or our procurement team)?
- Does Redwood support automatic pushes to an AP email (PDF) or do you require portal enrollment (API/token)?
- Our US subsidiary is tax-exempt; we'll need the invoices to include our Exempt ID and a tax-exempt flag.

For first month we'd prefer signed PDFs delivered to procurement@acme-corp.com with APTeam@acme-corp.com on CC while we confirm portal access.

AP Manager, Acme Industries
APTeam@acme-corp.com
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai (Jonas Weber)

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-28T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice routing and tax handling for Redwood account

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear details.

Short answers:
- Redwood will author the invoices.
- We support both workflows: (1) portal/API push using a short-lived onboarding token (recommended for automation) and (2) manual signed-PDF push to an AP inbox (acceptable as a fall-back).

Notes / questions for you so we can configure correctly:
1) Please confirm the exact remit-to name and Exempt ID to print on the invoice header.
2) For the signed PDFs: do you need a digital (DocuSign) signature or a PDF stamped by our billing engine?
3) If you opt for a portal token, we will generate a temporary token scoped to invoice delivery only; we can expire it after 14 days.

If you confirm "email push + CC for first two invoices" we'll schedule that immediately and follow up with a token if you decide to enroll permanently.

I'll loop in Kimberly to handle the token creation and tax tagging.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
